implementation_changes: V304 bit traces were changed from full-byte final-answer style to bit_serial_target_verification_trace_v2.

V304 dataset regenerated at artifacts/v304_solver_trace_distill_dataset/20260512T1430Z with train SHA 7935ff999cdd8318de67538922de3651170c59baa2664a10beac3334dfcf9082 and val SHA 2b06224afe035c5085798f4a4be27e764ffaebde3ff7eee11c558c0cd5bdd29d.
V286 tokenizer gate passed for V304 suffix-mode traces with real Nemotron tokenizer, zero prompt truncation, zero fallback masks and max token length 745.

items.action: Keep as background; do not drive training changes from this thread alone.
items.finding: Resource hub. The actionable signal is not algorithmic; comments and linked resources reinforce using official NeMo/Nemotron docs and not treating public notebooks/traces as authoritative without verification.
items.impact: No direct score gain; useful only as source index.
items.title: How to Get Started + resources

items.action: Keep final-answer suffix/boxed gates and avoid extra braces/noisy completions.
items.finding: Metric extraction changed around boxed answer handling and brace parsing.
items.impact: Submissions can differ only by formatting; local gates must preserve final answer extraction exactly.
items.title: Metric Update

items.action: Maintain exact binary string scorer and regression tests for bit outputs.
items.finding: Binary answers were corrected to exact-string comparison rather than float-like matching.
items.impact: Bit outputs must be exact 8-character binary strings; numeric coercion is invalid.
items.title: Rescore After Metric Update

items.action: Distill V302/V300 gains into adapter-only behavior; package gate remains adapter_config + safetensors only.
items.finding: Official submission path is a LoRA adapter package, rank constrained.
items.impact: Postprocessor/verifier gains are not directly submitable unless competition packaging allows them.
items.title: Official getting started / Discord

items.action: Use generated, deterministic, locally verifiable traces; record provenance in manifests.
items.finding: Thread discusses which external/model-generated data can be distilled; no universally safe shortcut is provided.
items.impact: Legal/rules risk if using closed-model outputs blindly.
items.title: Distillation legality discussion

items.action: Use only for trace design and held-out verifier research; no submit/full eval directly from gold-conditioned outputs.
items.finding: Symbolic solver uses the known answer as a constraint; it is a research oracle, not inference-time solver.
items.impact: Useful for understanding equation/symbolic latent rules and generating checked traces, but unsafe as direct predictor.
items.title: Gold-conditioned symbolic solver

items.action: Keep symbolic work CPU-only until no-loss gates prove a deployable rule.
items.finding: Finite examples can support multiple valid transformations; public DSL/LLM traces can regress held-out score.
items.impact: Broad symbolic trace ingestion is high risk.
items.title: Symbol transformation ambiguity

items.action: Use as blueprint for V304/V305: bit-serial traces now implemented; next add full THK-style pair/stride/bitsum scan and numeric equation scan-stop audit.
items.finding: Most actionable playbook: bit is solved as eight independent boolean functions with ordered gates, bit-serial computation and target verification; equation numeric/symbolic uses scan orders, second-example verification and hard-stop behavior.
items.impact: Explains why V303 answer/full-byte traces failed and why V304 moved to bit_serial_target_verification_trace_v2.
items.title: Answers To Everything Data

items.action: Keep GRPO as P2 only after SFT/verifier traces show weak gains and loss/logprob bottlenecks.
items.finding: GRPO may help after cold-start SFT, but evidence is debated and compute-heavy.
items.impact: Not the next move under small HF budget.
items.title: GRPO is must debate

items.action: Add min-logprob audit before long HF runs; keep V304 traces under 1300 tokens and use weak gates as primary success metric.
items.finding: Tong emphasizes deterministic CoT, token budget, min-logprob inspection, loss masking, rare-operation coverage and training-serving alignment; winning target was around 0.877 with bit as key driver.
items.impact: Loss alone is insufficient; inspect token-level low-confidence points and keep traces short/learnable.
items.title: SFT to maximize minimum logprob

items.action: Compare family-level artifacts and repeat weak/full where affordable before submit.
items.finding: Participants saw score drift from metric update and vLLM behavior.
items.impact: Public 0.86 plateau can hide small gains/losses.
items.title: Score drop / metric nondeterminism

items.action: Optional P2: mine base-model completions only for prompt/logprob diagnostics, not labels.
items.finding: Base-model generations over train are available from Tong; useful as diagnostic/logprob reference, not a direct new solver.
items.impact: Can help find prompts where the model already has priors vs where training must teach exact algorithms.
items.title: Base model visualization

items.action: Cap oversampling, preserve replay, check duplicate assistant conflicts, use low LR and stop on weak regression.
items.finding: Correct synthetic solver data can lower leaderboard if traces are hard to learn, duplicate/conflicting, oversampled, or format-shift the baseline.
items.impact: Directly explains V303/V292 risks and imposes gates on V304+.
items.title: Synthetic CoT accuracy -> LB drop

items.action: Document as no-op.
items.finding: Prize/logistics thread only.
items.impact: No score/ACC signal.
items.title: Open Progress Prize question

items.action: Use as design confirmation only.
items.finding: Donald claims factories and structured traces for all categories but provides no public artifact.
items.impact: Supports solver-trace direction, but cannot be imported as evidence/data.
items.title: Deterministic solvers compute partner

items.action: Repeat weak eval or require bigger-than-noise local family gains before submit.
items.finding: vLLM nondeterminism can change scores even at temperature 0.
items.impact: Small deltas require controlled local evaluation, not one public score.
items.title: 0.84-0.86 variance with winning zip

items.action: No implementation change.
items.finding: Leaderboard/prize timing; no algorithmic content.
items.impact: No score/ACC action.
items.title: Midpoint cutoff logistics

items.action: Build CPU-only V305 numeric guess fallback audit before any equation-heavy training.
items.finding: Some numeric equation cases have query operators absent from examples; fallback can depend on output length, reversal, sign and learned priors rather than pure deduction.
items.impact: Equation_transform +4 local postprocessor gains are plausible but must be no-loss gated.
items.title: Numeric equations ambiguity

items.action: Keep +1/+2 no-loss gates; do not submit unvalidated broad changes.
items.finding: Participants infer public LB may be only a few hundred examples, so one or two correct answers can move rank.
items.impact: Micro-gains matter, but they must avoid hidden regressions.
items.title: Public leaderboard size

items.action: Use H200 short smoke with strict GPU/memory and checkpoint weak gates; no long run without signal.
items.finding: Rank-32 LoRA at 8192 context is memory heavy; H200/microbatch planning matters.
items.impact: Long traces and broad datasets can burn HF budget quickly.
items.title: Rank32 LoRA memory at 8192

items.action: Use simple bit unit tests as a cheap pretrain/gate source only if provenance/no-overlap is clean.
items.finding: Base model is only about half-correct on simple one-operation bit transforms.
items.impact: Bit requires explicit SFT/verifier traces; relying on base reasoning is not enough.
items.title: Unit testing simple bit transforms

items.action: Route equation work through scan/verifier/fallback rules, not LLM prompting.
items.finding: Community confirms bit and equation are the hardest; one participant decoded many bit samples but still lacked reproducible equation reasoning.
items.impact: Supports prioritizing deterministic equation audit rather than generic prompting.
items.title: Equation Transformation reasoning

items.action: Add ambiguity/no-loss checks to bit solvers and do not train on unresolved ambiguous labels.
items.finding: Some bit examples are underdetermined; multiple rules fit examples but predict different queries.
items.impact: Example-fit alone is unsafe; target verification and conservative rule ordering are necessary.
items.title: Bit transformations uniquely determined?

items.action: Keep V304 traces compact; validate prompt masking and family replay before GPU spend.
items.finding: Short CoT beat longer CoT for one participant; rank32/lower LR did not help without better data/masking.
items.impact: More tokens/rank is not a solution by itself.
items.title: Stuck at 0.56 SFT approach

items.action: Use low-risk smoke, min-logprob/token audit, replay anchoring, oversampling cap and early kill-switch.
items.finding: Algorithmic accuracy 95.8% still failed to beat 0.85 due learnability, oversampling, LR/gradient saturation and masking; traces under about 1300 tokens were reported as more practical.
items.impact: This is the main training-risk warning for V304/V305.
items.title: Better dataset scored worse

items.action: Keep as supporting note for trace compression.
items.finding: Raises token-budget tradeoff; no concrete answer in thread.
items.impact: No direct new data, but consistent with compact trace policy.
items.title: CoT length on bit

items.action: Implement V305/V306 THK-style pair/stride/bitsum trace generator and evaluate before long SFT.
items.finding: Tong describes a bit algorithm solving 1364/1602 train bit puzzles using pair-of-input-bit iteration, bitsum hash, stride matching and compact token budget. Comment reports even stronger bit/numeric equation solver numbers, unverified by us.
items.impact: Best public blueprint for turning bit 135/160 into higher adapter behavior. V304 only implements target verification, not full bitsum/stride scan yet.
items.title: Strategy to solve 85% of bit manipulation

items.action: Add numeric/equation fallback audit with sign, length, reversal and same-op absence features.
items.finding: Equation/cryptarithm guess cases may be information-theoretic unless priors or output-format clues are learned.
items.impact: Equation improvements need fallback priors and confidence routing, not only exact-rule deduction.
items.title: Missing pieces: equation and cryptarithm

items.action: Keep V221 weak/full official-like contracts; do not trust ad hoc local CV.
items.finding: Local SFT/CV can be misleading when category distribution is nonuniform; high local bit/equation subsets may not translate to LB.
items.impact: Need stratified official-like gates.
items.title: RLVR worth it?

next_actions: Commit and push discussion audit, V304 dataset/gate, and roadmap updates.
Before a paid HF run, implement/verify a HF preflight gate: dataset hash, tokenizer suffix mode, adapter path/config, GPU/memory, replay/duplicate conflict, weak kill-switch.
Run one short H200 V304 smoke only; continue only if weak bit improves above 135/160 or equation above 56/155 without side-family regression.
Build CPU-only V305 THK bitsum/stride and numeric equation fallback audits before any longer train.
